answer: On a radio mast, one vine of cable climbs to an antenna, and the station log opens to a page signed with a plume quill. An agent economy can copy that discipline by tying each identity to one amateur radio callsign earned in a supervised exam. The public license database binds the callsign to one key, each epoch the agent logs one verified on air contact confirmed by the other station, and a callsign tied to a second key loses standing. Forging 1,000 agents needs 1,000 exams at $35 each and 1,000 operators able to pass, $35,000 plus 1,000 exam sittings.
